title: What is Qualitative Interviewing?
abstract: This book makes clear the procedures and practices surrounding qualitative interviewing. Qualitative interviews are a critical part of qualitative research, but understandings of what it means to carry out interviews have shifted over time. This book provides the latest studies and practical guidance on how to cater for a broad range of research. It shows researchers and students how to begin with key questions and theories and the best interviewing tactic to take. What is Qualitative Interviewing? addresses the changes brought by new technologies as well as enduring issues such as asking and listening, the implications of power dynamics, and the broader social relations for research and interviewer-interviewee relations.

Full narrative

What is Qualitative Interviewing? by Rosalind Edwards and Janet Holland was published by Bloomsbury Publishing Plc. in 2013. Conceptually, the work connects to Interview, Qualitative research, Qualitative analysis, Key (lock) and Engineering ethics.

OpenAlex records 894 citations. That places it in the top 1% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2020 with 107 citing works. Notable citing venues include Nordic Academic Press eBooks, Unisa Institutional Repository (University of South Africa) and Sustainability. The citing works include 582 journal articles, 142 dissertations and 75 book chapters. They come from 40 countries, led by the United Kingdom, the United States and Germany.

It has been downloaded 21,069 times via OAPEN. Open Library reports a combined count of 5 reading logs and catalog editions. Its subject matter aligns with Quality Education among the Sustainable Development Goals.
